fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Jason Lindgren is the host of Secrets of Saturn and co-host of Crrow777 Radio. As a talented musician and dedicated researcher in the pursuit of Truth, Jason is just the type of person we like best on InnerVerse: jovial, knowledgeable, imaginative and interesting. This was a whirlwind conversation that covered a lot of ground, including the occult aspects of modern commerce and money, the monetary EL-ites (elites) of the world and their relationship to Saturn, the 52 year cycles of society, mind control, the fictional nature of America's legal system, manipulation of the music industry, and more.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Comic Books, Star Wars and the Modern Pantheon", "body": "Chance draws on Chris Knowles and his book Our Gods Wear Spandex to argue that comic book heroes are a new pantheon, old archetypes given fresh faces, and shows off the Spider-Man tattoo he got for its motto about power and responsibility. Jason counters that writers once had to respect the lore, and says Disney, under Kathleen Kennedy, threw that away by turning Luke Skywalker into a broken old man and killing off Han Solo. Chance reads Luke as lux, the light walking across the sky, and wonders why anyone needs a 100 year plan for Star Wars, while Jason hears the sun in the name Rey."}, {"title": "Light, Dark and the War on the Middle", "body": "Chance argues that darkness is half of the yin-yang rather than evil, and that true evil is the distortion of nature's harmony through human artifice. He contrasts equality of opportunity with equality in misery, and describes commerce as a kind of war, tying martial and maritime to the same root. Jason separates capitalism, which he supports, from corporatism, pointing to small shops shut down while big box stores stayed open. Chance then frames the moment as a war on the middle class, the most psychologically healthy layer of any society, and plays on police as pole ice."}, {"title": "Biocapitalism, Social Credit and Video Games", "body": "Chance lays out biocapitalism, where machines do the producing and people drift toward basic income or the gig economy, all shaped by lessons learned from video games. Jason says social credit already exists in China and parts of Australia and points to scoring on a site called MyLife. He notes that games outearn Hollywood and that screen refresh rates can induce a hypnotic state. Chance describes an Assassin's Creed storyline that blames the player for a plague, recalls running a World of Warcraft guild, and calls gaming a surrogate womb, while Jason urges moderation and a disciplined mind."}, {"title": "The Pandemic Through a Skeptic's Lens", "body": "Jason describes how he and Crow brought Dr. Andy Kaufman, an accredited doctor who questions the official story, to a much wider audience, and argues that a real quarantine isolates the sick rather than shutting down whole economies. He treats mask mandates as a compliance test, and Chance calls them a symbolic ritual, and the two tie masks back to the masked villains of Star Wars, Darth Vader and Kylo Ren. Chance adds that the crisis began in March, which he says was the true start of the year, and Jason backs this up by pointing out that October takes its name from the number eight."}, {"title": "Sky Clock Knowledge, Freemasonry and Symbols", "body": "Chance recommends the book Spirit Whirled, which traces the sun's journey through the zodiac across many religions. Jason suggests secret societies began by guarding sky clock knowledge, like a shaman who can predict eclipses. He walks through the Masonic degrees, from the blue lodge and the Scottish Rite to Shriners and the honorary 33rd, and describes the checkerboard floor and twin columns of a Masonic hall as the Temple of Solomon. Chance links the temple and words like circuit and Galilee to the sky clock, and Jason insists that no symbol or number is bad in itself, only the intent behind it."}]
